From dbdb442218cd9d613adeab31a88ac973f22c4873 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Pei Xiao <xiaopei01@kylinos.cn>
Date: Wed, 29 Oct 2025 10:40:16 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] iio: adc: at91-sama5d2_adc: Fix potential use-after-free in
 sama5d2_adc driver

at91_adc_interrupt can call at91_adc_touch_data_handler function
to start the work by schedule_work(&st->touch_st.workq).

If we remove the module which will call at91_adc_remove to
make cleanup, it will free indio_dev through iio_device_unregister but
quite a bit later. While the work mentioned above will be used. The
sequence of operations that may lead to a UAF bug is as follows:

CPU0                                      CPU1

                                     | at91_adc_workq_handler
at91_adc_remove                      |
iio_device_unregister(indio_dev)     |
//free indio_dev a bit later         |
                                     | iio_push_to_buffers(indio_dev)
                                     | //use indio_dev

Fix it by ensuring that the work is canceled before proceeding with
the cleanup in at91_adc_remove.

Fixes: 23ec2774f1cc ("iio: adc: at91-sama5d2_adc: add support for position and pressure channels")
Signed-off-by: Pei Xiao <xiaopei01@kylinos.cn>
Cc: <Stable@vger.kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Jonathan Cameron <Jonathan.Cameron@huawei.com>

diff --git a/drivers/iio/adc/at91-sama5d2_adc.c b/drivers/iio/adc/at91-sama5d2_adc.c
index b4c36e6a7490..aa4ba3f5a506 100644
--- a/drivers/iio/adc/at91-sama5d2_adc.c
+++ b/drivers/iio/adc/at91-sama5d2_adc.c
@@ -2481,6 +2481,7 @@ static void at91_adc_remove(struct platform_device *pdev)
 	struct at91_adc_state *st = iio_priv(indio_dev);
 
 	iio_device_unregister(indio_dev);
+	cancel_work_sync(&st->touch_st.workq);
 
 	at91_adc_dma_disable(st);
 
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of Modifications

### Modifications in Each File

**File:** `drivers/iio/adc/at91-sama5d2_adc.c`

- **Added:** `cancel_work_sync(&st->touch_st.workq);` after `iio_device_unregister(indio_dev);` and before `at91_adc_dma_disable(st);` in the `at91_adc_remove` function.

### Relationship Between Modifications

The patch prevents a potential use-after-free bug by ensuring that any pending or running touch‑related work (`touch_st.workq`) is fully cancelled before the core IIO device (`indio_dev`) is freed during module removal. The work function (`at91_adc_workq_handler`) may access `indio_dev` via `iio_push_to_buffers()`, so canceling it synchronously after unregistering the device but before deallocating the device structure eliminates the race condition.

Here is the commit message:
iio: adc: at91-sama5d2_adc: Fix potential use-after-free in
 sama5d2_adc driver

at91_adc_interrupt can call at91_adc_touch_data_handler function
to start the work by schedule_work(&st->touch_st.workq).

If we remove the module which will call at91_adc_remove to
make cleanup, it will free indio_dev through iio_device_unregister but
quite a bit later. While the work mentioned above will be used. The
sequence of operations that may lead to a UAF bug is as follows:

CPU0                                      CPU1

                                     | at91_adc_workq_handler
at91_adc_remove                      |
iio_device_unregister(indio_dev)     |
//free indio_dev a bit later         |
                                     | iio_push_to_buffers(indio_dev)
                                     | //use indio_dev

Fix it by ensuring that the work is canceled before proceeding with
the cleanup in at91_adc_remove.

Fixes: 23ec2774f1cc ("iio: adc: at91-sama5d2_adc: add support for position and pressure channels")
Signed-off-by: Pei Xiao <xiaopei01@kylinos.cn>
Cc: <Stable@vger.kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Jonathan Cameron <Jonathan.Cameron@huawei.com>

Here is the root cause:
The `at91_adc_remove` function calls `iio_device_unregister` which frees `indio_dev`, but does not cancel the work queue (`touch_st.workq`) that may still be pending or executing. This work queue, scheduled from the interrupt handler, later accesses `indio_dev` (e.g., via `iio_push_to_buffers`), leading to a use-after-free.

Here is the patch:
 
 static void at91_adc_remove(struct platform_device *pdev)
 {
 	struct iio_dev *indio_dev = platform_get_drvdata(pdev);
 	struct at91_adc_state *st = iio_priv(indio_dev);
 
 	iio_device_unregister(indio_dev);
+	cancel_work_sync(&st->touch_st.workq);
 
 	at91_adc_dma_disable(st);
 
 	pm_runtime_disable(st->dev);
 	pm_runtime_set_suspended(st->dev);
 	clk_disable_unprepare(st->per_clk);
 
 	regulator_disable(st->vref);
 	regulator_disable(st->reg);
 }

This work queue, scheduled from the interrupt handler, later accesses `indio_dev` (e.g., via `iio_push_to_buffers`), leading to a use-after-free.

Code statements information:
The code statements that lead to the bug are:
iio_device_unregister(indio_dev);
schedule_work(&st->touch_st.workq);
iio_push_to_buffers(indio_dev);
Reason:
The `at91_adc_remove` function calls `iio_device_unregister` which frees `indio_dev`, but does not cancel the work queue (`touch_st.workq`). The work queue is scheduled from the interrupt handler via `schedule_work`, and when it later executes `iio_push_to_buffers(indio_dev)`, it accesses the already freed memory, causing a use-after-free.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
+	cancel_work_sync(&st->touch_st.workq);
Reason:
Adding `cancel_work_sync` before `iio_device_unregister` ensures that any pending or executing work item is completed or canceled. This prevents the work handler from accessing `indio_dev` after it has been freed, eliminating the use-after-free vulnerability.
